evidence.source: Marazzi 2011, The Plant Press, Nectarless Flowers and Leaves with Extrafloral Nectaries
evidence.result: Species-level field observation records small bees visiting S. covesii and audible buzz visits; Senna flowers are described as pollen-reward systems in which sonication ejects pollen onto bees and pollen that escapes grooming is transferred to conspecific stigmas.

evidence.source: Felger & Rutman 2015, Flora of southwestern Arizona Part 14
evidence.result: S. covesii has seven fertile poricidal stamens and flowers are buzz-pollinated by bees.
S. covesii is documented as a poricidal species that conceals pollen within anthers, consistent with pollen as the bee-collected floral resource.
